figures.finding: Western Australia's laws, as in force there from time to time and including its common law, are in force on Christmas Island, subject to the Island's Ordinances, which may amend or suspend them; so WA's majority and child-employment law are the Island's (no suspending Ordinance was looked for).

law: Commonwealth Acts that extend to the Territory

sources.said: Subject to this section, section 8G and Part IVA, Western Australian laws are in force in the Territory.
An Ordinance may suspend the operation in the Territory of a law in force in the Territory under subsection (1) for such period as is specified in the Ordinance.
A Western Australian law: (a) is a law in force in Western Australia from time to time; and (b) includes a principle or rule of common law or equity that is part of the law of Western Australia;

figures.finding: No one may employ a child under fifteen in a business carried on for profit, but the rule doesn't apply to a child employed in a dramatic or musical performance or other entertainment or in making an advertisement; no permit, hours or schooling rule attaches; the CEO may by notice prohibit or limit a particular child's employment where the child's wellbeing is likely to be jeopardised; the exception names performing only, so a child writing or directing for profit falls under the general bar under fifteen.

sources.said: A person must not employ a child under 15 years of age in a business, trade or occupation carried on for profit.
Section 190(1) and (3) do not apply if the child is employed in a dramatic or musical performance or other form of entertainment or in the making of an advertisement.

figures.finding: Only an individual of at least eighteen may be appointed a director of a company registered under the Corporations Act; the Act's own area is the States and internal Territories (external Territories only for parts of Chapter 7 by regulation), so a Christmas Island producer's company would be one registered under it, a reading.
